Not so many suggestions at the moment, hovewer, an interesting one
maybe the following:
keep in your hand some Compel the Spirit (from Dark Sovereign), until
your library will be empty, at that point have an
Akhenaten in play or a Kherebutu (or both); have him burned to burn a
proper vampire (either a Follower of Set for Akhenaten or a Tremere for
Kherebutu),
take back the Mummy (for free) from your ash heap with a Superior
Compel the Spirit, then again
burn another proper Vamp by burning again the Compeled Mummy,
then again take it back with another the Superior Compel the Spirit,
then again burn a Vamp..and so on until your hand will be reduced to
zero.
At that point you may Withdraw from the game ending up in glory.
It's not a very good or functional strategy, but at least a very
original one (providing your actual prey is playing Tremere or
Followers of Set).
It would work a bit better if you manage to have a very large hand size
at the moment you have your library empty (Elder library, Cassandra
Magus Prime amd so on).
You must have your cript library, else the Mummies had to be reshuffled
in your library and the superior Compel could not work.
Wait a bit, and you'll find more interesting uses for the Mummies.
Best.
Aemilianus, Prince of Rome

This would first of all require other people to be playing those clans -

But unfortunately, here it breaks down.

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
On Sat, 18 Mar 2000 tetragr...@my-deja.com wrote:
> PLEASE, read the maiusc above first.

I did read that your library was empty - I do not know what "maiusc" is.
The mummies still go into your library, to the best of my knowledge - it
simply has no cards in it, but still exists (such that a hypothetical
effect "Move 5 cards from your ash-heap to your library" would work even
if your library were empty).

That way, Compel the Spirit is still unplayable, as the mummies are either
in your library, or in your hand, but not in your ash-heap, unless you can
discard them there (which makes a somewhat tenuous combo, requiring a
player to be playing specific clans, even more tenuous, since you need a
discard mechanism in play).

If you still think I'm missing something, it would be useful if you would
explain your point, rather than just SHOUTING BY USING LOTS OF CAPITAL
LETTERS.

--

James Coupe

Messages.Author: Halcyan 2
Messages.Body:
>That way, Compel the Spirit is still unplayable, as the mummies are either
>in your library, or in your hand, but not in your ash-heap, unless you can
>discard them there (which makes a somewhat tenuous combo, requiring a
>player to be playing specific clans, even more tenuous, since you need a
>discard mechanism in play).

Sorry to burst your bubble, but "discarding" them (as opposed to getting them
killed) will violate the requirements of Compel the Spirit, which needs a
retainer/ally that "has been burned since your last turn." Since discarded
cards aren't considered in play or anything, the mummies would be stuck in the
ash heap (unless you use Carlotta or Whispers).

Halcyan 2

The empty library exists. Mummies will be returned to it.
[SFC 17-SEP-1996].

This can be deduced by considering the parallel with the ash heap:

What do you do with your first discard, when your ash heap is
empty (i.e., does an empty ash heap exist to receive cards)?

Messages.Body:
On Mon, 20 Mar 2000 16:01:59 GMT, tetragr...@my-deja.com wrote:

>Ok, got that (and thanks).

>(if he is burned) "shuffle him in your library".

>since there are no card in the library to "shuffle" the actual Mummy in.

Of course you could. Put your card in the empty library. Now shuffle
your 1 card, over and over, 'til you gain a reasonably random order.

See? The verb "shuffle" does not require a minimum number of cards -
just that there be a card.

> If we are speaking about "shuffling",
> the term alone clearly refers to more than
> one component to be "shuffled".

No. The one component being shuffled is your library.
"Shuffle your library".
It means to arrange the cards in your library in
a random order - to randomize your library. [DCI 21]

With only one card "randomized" into the existing
zero cards in your library, the random order is
as "random" as pulling a name out of a hat with
only one name in it, but that is the best that
can be achieved under the circumstances.

> I can "shuffle" one piece of "something" only if another piece
> of "something" is at hand, at least in my Italian,
> maybe in english is different.

You can "suffle" ("randomize") a deck of one card. There is
only one outcome of such an event, but it is still shuffled.

> If it is not, game logic should not change language logic.
> Then, if i want a burned Mummy to be "shuffled" in an empty library,
> the actual question is to change the Mummies' text.
> instead of:
>
> "If Akhenaten (or Kherebutu) is burned, shuffle him in your library".
>

> it should read:

>
> "If Akhenaten (or Kherebutu) is burned, PUT him in your library
> (reshuffle afterwards)"

These are equivalent phrases.
The result is the same.
